answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume, no buffer, and a hard 14-day expiry, a full vendor switch (memory_c2) carries qualification and ramp risk that conflicts with the 'no increase in delivery risk' constraint. Negotiating terms with the incumbent (memory_c4: benchmarking recovered margin on price and payment terms; memory_c6: multi-year volume pricing) is the most credible path to approach the 18% mandate without disrupting supply, and memory_c1 shows renewals have been stable. I want to verify memory_c4 to confirm the renegotiation actually delivered the claimed savings before relying on it. Fallback if negotiation stalls: renew at current terms to avoid a supply gap, then revisit dual-sourcing (memory_c3) next cycle.
